title: Summarise call-level exclusions into a manuscript-ready paragraph — mysterycall_exclusion_summary
code: ## --- minimal runnable example (base R only) ------------------------------- reasons <- c(   "Able to contact",   "Phone not answered or busy signal on repeat calls",   "Went to voicemail",   "Number contacted did not correspond to expected office/specialty",   "Physician referral required before scheduling appointment",   "Not accepting new patients",   "Greater than 5 minutes on hold" ) n_each <- c(120L, 40L, 30L, 10L, 15L, 20L, 5L)  df <- data.frame(   call_id               = seq_len(sum(n_each)),   reason_for_exclusions = rep(reasons, n_each),   stringsAsFactors      = FALSE )  result <- mysterycall_exclusion_summary(df) print(result)       # prints the prose paragraph #> A total of 240 phone calls were made. Of these, 80 (33.3%) calls were unsuccessful connections, including calls in which the phone was not answered or the caller received a busy signal (n = 40), calls that went to voicemail (n = 30), and calls for which the number reached did not correspond to the expected office or specialty (n = 10). The remaining 160 (66.7%) calls resulted in a successful connection with office staff. Among successfully connected calls, 15 offices required a physician referral before an appointment could be scheduled, 20 offices were not accepting new patients, and 5 calls were placed on hold for more than 5 minutes. After applying all exclusion criteria, 120 (50.0%) calls were included in the final analysis.  result$table        # tabyl-style counts #>             category #> 1           included #> 2 phone_not_answered #> 3          voicemail #> 4       wrong_number #> 5  referral_required #> 6      not_accepting #> 7            on_hold #>                                                              label   n #> 1                                             Included in analysis 120 #> 2                Phone not answered or busy signal on repeat calls  40 #> 3                                                Went to voicemail  30 #> 4 Number contacted did not correspond to expected office/specialty  10 #> 5        Physician referral required before scheduling appointment  15 #> 6                                       Not accepting new patients  20 #> 7                                   Greater than 5 minutes on hold   5 #>         pct #> 1 50.000000 #> 2 16.666667 #> 3 12.500000 #> 4  4.166667 #> 5  6.250000 #> 6  8.333333 #> 7  2.083333  ## --- custom exclusion values (different study coding scheme) -------------- df2 <- df names(df2)[2] <- "call_outcome" result2 <- mysterycall_exclusion_summary(   data          = df2,   exclusion_col = "call_outcome",   inclusion_value = "Able to contact",   exclusion_categories = c(     phone_not_answered = "Phone not answered or busy signal on repeat calls",     voicemail          = "Went to voicemail",     wrong_number       = "Number contacted did not correspond to expected office/specialty",     referral_required  = "Physician referral required before scheduling appointment",     not_accepting      = "Not accepting new patients",     on_hold            = "Greater than 5 minutes on hold"   ) ) cat(result2$paragraph) #> A total of 240 phone calls were made. Of these, 80 (33.3%) calls were unsuccessful connections, including calls in which the phone was not answered or the caller received a busy signal (n = 40), calls that went to voicemail (n = 30), and calls for which the number reached did not correspond to the expected office or specialty (n = 10). The remaining 160 (66.7%) calls resulted in a successful connection with office staff. Among successfully connected calls, 15 offices required a physician referral before an appointment could be scheduled, 20 offices were not accepting new patients, and 5 calls were placed on hold for more than 5 minutes. what: Extract the intraclass correlation coefficient from a fitted model — mysterycall_icc
title: Extract the intraclass correlation coefficient from a fitted model — mysterycall_icc
text: Computes ICC physician random intercept using latent-variable method (Nakagawa & Schielzeth 2010). ICC quantifies proportion total outcome variance attributable -physician clustering, justifies use GLMM simple GLM.

title: Extract the intraclass correlation coefficient from a fitted model — mysterycall_icc
code: mysterycall_icc(model_result, conf_level = 0.95, n_boot = 0L, seed = NULL)

title: Extract the intraclass correlation coefficient from a fitted model — mysterycall_icc
text: model_result mysterycall_poisson_model mysterycall_nb_model object returned mysterycall_poisson_model() mysterycall_nb_model(). conf_level Numeric. Confidence level bootstrap CI. Default 0.95. Used n_boot > 0. n_boot Integer. Number bootstrap replicates confidence interval. Default 0L (bootstrap; CI c(NA, NA)). Values 500-2000 recommended publication. seed Integer NULL. Random seed bootstrap reproducibility. Default NULL.

title: Extract the intraclass correlation coefficient from a fitted model — mysterycall_icc
text: list class mysterycall_icc elements: icc Numeric. ICC point estimate. sigma2_u Numeric. Physician random-intercept variance log scale. method Character. "latent_variable_poisson" "latent_variable_nb". ci Numeric vector length 2. Bootstrap percentile CI, c(NA, NA) n_boot = 0. n_boot Integer. Number bootstrap replicates used. interpretation Character. One-sentence plain-language summary. model_class Character. Class model_result.

title: Extract the intraclass correlation coefficient from a fitted model — mysterycall_icc
text: Poisson models: $$\text{ICC} = \frac{\sigma^2_u}{\sigma^2_u + \pi^2/3}$$ negative binomial models: $$\text{ICC} = \frac{\sigma^2_u}{\sigma^2_u + \psi_1(1/\theta) + \pi^2/3}$$ \(\sigma^2_u\) physician random-intercept variance, \(\pi^2/3\) logistic-distribution variance (latent-variable approximation), \(\psi_1\) trigamma function.

title: Extract the intraclass correlation coefficient from a fitted model — mysterycall_icc
text: Nakagawa S, Schielzeth H (2010). general simple method obtaining R^2 generalized linear mixed-effects models. Methods Ecology Evolution 4(2):133-142. doi:10.1111/j.2041-210x.2012.00261.x

title: Extract the intraclass correlation coefficient from a fitted model — mysterycall_icc

title: Multiple imputation by chained equations for missing call outcomes — mysterycall_impute_calls
text: Rubin's rules (1987) \(\bar{Q} = \frac{1}{m} \sum_{=1}^{m} \hat{\beta}_i\) (pooled estimate) \(\bar{U} = \frac{1}{m} \sum_{=1}^{m} \hat{\text{SE}}_i^2\) (within-imputation variance) \(B = \frac{1}{m-1} \sum_{=1}^{m} (\hat{\beta}_i - \bar{Q})^2\) (-imputation variance) \(T = \bar{U} + \left(1 + \frac{1}{m}\right) B\) (total variance) Degrees freedom: \(\nu = (m-1) \left(1 + \frac{\bar{U}}{(1+1/m) B}\right)^2\) Fraction missing information: \(\text{FMI} = \frac{B + B/m}{T}\)

code: m <- mysterycall_materials_methods(   callers    = c("Lizeth", "Merilyn", "Jessica"),   irb_number = "COMIRB-2024-001" ) print(m) #> === Materials & Methods Section === #>  #> -- caller standardization -- #> Three female research team members (Jessica, Lizeth, and Merilyn) were trained #> as standardized callers prior to data collection. All callers used an identical #> verbatim call script (see Appendix A); no improvisation was permitted. Callers #> identified themselves as prospective new patients, provided the scripted #> clinical complaint, stated their insurance type when asked, and requested the #> first available appointment offered. Calls were placed during standard business #> hours (Monday through Friday, 9:00 am - 4:00 pm local time). [Inter-caller #> reliability results pending - run mysterycall_caller_reliability()] #>  #>  #> -- call spacing -- #> To minimize scheduler recognition across repeated calls to the same practice, a #> minimum interval of 24 hours elapsed between any two calls to the same #> physician's office. Caller assignment was rotated systematically across #> physicians and conditions to prevent caller-by-condition confounding. #>  #>  #> -- appointment definition -- #> The primary outcome was the number of calendar days from the date of the call #> to the date of the first available appointment offered. Callers recorded the #> appointment date offered but did not confirm or accept any appointment. Calls #> in which no appointment was offered were recorded as unsuccessful and excluded #> from wait-time analyses. #>  #>  #> -- physician selection -- #> Eligible physicians were board-certified Female Pelvic Medicine and #> Reconstructive Surgery (FPMRS) specialists identified through a random sample #> of the patient-facing physician directory (voicesforpfd.org). [N physicians - #> confirm from data]. Physicians were not contacted in advance and were unaware #> of their inclusion in the study. #>  #>  #> -- missing data -- #> [N complete] of [N total] calls ([%]) had a complete appointment date. To #> evaluate whether calls with missing appointment dates differed systematically #> from those with complete data, physician and call characteristics were compared #> between groups (see Supplemental Table [X] for the missing data analysis). #>  #>  #> -- business days -- #> Although business days are the preferred scheduling metric, calendar days were #> used as the primary unit because federal holiday calendars vary by state and #> institution. A sensitivity analysis using business days (excluding weekends and #> U.S. federal holidays) is reported in Supplemental Table [X]. #>  #>  #> -- irb -- #> The study was approved by the Colorado Multiple Institutional Review Board #> (COMIRB) (Protocol No. COMIRB-2024-001). Given that office staff were unaware #> they were being observed, the board granted a waiver of informed consent, #> classifying the study as minimal risk. No protected health information was #> collected, and no actual appointments were scheduled. The verbatim call script #> is reproduced in Appendix A. #>  #>  #> Items requiring manual input: #>   [ ] Inter-caller reliability results (provide caller_col and outcome_col) #>   [ ] N physicians (provide physician_col) #>   [ ] N total calls (provide data) #>   [ ] N complete calls (provide outcome_col) #>   [ ] Supplemental table number for missing data analysis #>   [ ] Supplemental table number for business-days sensitivity analysis

code: mysterycall_methods_paragraph(   n_physicians  = 369,   n_cities      = 10,   specialties   = c("otolaryngology", "neurotology"),   insurance_types = c("Medicaid", "Blue Cross Blue Shield") ) #> [1] "A mystery-caller audit methodology was employed. A total of 369 physicians representing otolaryngology and neurotology were identified from publicly available directories across 10 cities and states in the United States. Mystery callers posed as new patients insured with Medicaid and Blue Cross Blue Shield and contacted each physician's office to request the earliest available new-patient appointment. Calls were standardized and completed within one week of each other. The primary outcome was business days until a new-patient appointment. All analyses were performed using R (R Foundation for Statistical Computing). A multilevel Poisson regression model with physician random intercepts was fit using the lme4 package to estimate incidence rate ratios (IRR) for the primary outcomes."  mysterycall_methods_paragraph(   n_physicians    = 216,   n_cities        = 12,   specialties     = "otolaryngology",   model_family    = "negative_binomial" ) #> [1] "A mystery-caller audit methodology was employed. A total of 216 physicians representing otolaryngology were identified from publicly available directories across 12 cities and states in the United States. Mystery callers posed as new patients insured with Medicaid and commercial insurance and contacted each physician's office to request the earliest available new-patient appointment. Calls were standardized and completed within one week of each other. The primary outcome was business days until a new-patient appointment. All analyses were performed using R (R Foundation for Statistical Computing). A multilevel negative binomial regression model with physician random intercepts was fit using the glmmTMB package to account for overdispersion in appointment wait times and estimate incidence rate ratios (IRR)."

title: Simulate power for a negative binomial mixed model — mysterycall_nb_power
text: n_physicians Integer. Number physicians (clusters) per group. calls_per_physician Integer. Number mystery calls per physician. Default 2L (one Medicaid, one reference insurance). irr Numeric. IRR detect (e.g. 0.75 means 25% fewer days intervention group). Must positive. theta Numeric. Negative binomial dispersion parameter. Higher values mean less overdispersion (Poisson limit theta -> Inf). Use $theta pilot mysterycall_nb_model() fit, literature-based estimate. Default 2.0 (moderate overdispersion typical wait-time data). baseline_mean Numeric. Expected mean wait days reference group. Default 21 (three weeks). sigma_u Numeric. Standard deviation physician-level random intercept (log scale). Default 0.3 (typical specialty scheduling). alpha Numeric. Type error rate. Default 0.05. n_sim Integer. title: Sample-size calculation for a Poisson mystery caller study — mysterycall_poisson_power
text: irr Numeric. minimum detectable incidence rate ratio. Must positive equal 1. lambda_ref Numeric. Expected mean wait time (days) reference insurance group (e.g. BCBS). Must positive. alpha Numeric. Two-sided type error rate. Default 0.05. power Numeric. Desired statistical power (1 - beta). Default 0.80. both_arms Logical. TRUE, provider called insurance types (paired design), halving total providers needed. Default TRUE. icc Numeric [0, 1). Intra-cluster correlation providers clustered (e.g. practice). Applied design-effect inflation: n * (1 + (m - 1) * icc) m calls_per_cluster. Default 0 (clustering adjustment). calls_per_cluster Integer. Average calls per cluster, used icc > 0. Default 2L.

title: Sample-size calculation for a Poisson mystery caller study — mysterycall_poisson_power
text: named list elements: n_per_arm Providers needed per insurance arm. n_total Total providers needed. n_total_calls Total calls placed (= n_per_arm * 2 n_total * 2 paired design). irr, lambda_ref, lambda_trt Input parameters plus derived treatment-arm mean. alpha, power Input parameters. design_effect Inflation factor icc > 0.

title: Sample-size calculation for a Poisson mystery caller study — mysterycall_poisson_power
text: sample-size formula derived score test comparing two independent Poisson rates \(\lambda_0\) (reference arm, e.g. BCBS) \(\lambda_1 = \text{IRR} \times \lambda_0\) (treatment arm, e.g. Medicaid): $$n = \frac{(z_{\alpha/2} + z_\beta)^2 \left(\frac{1}{\lambda_0} + \frac{1}{\lambda_1}\right)}{(\log \text{IRR})^2}$$ gives providers per arm. Total providers = n * 2. provider called insurance types (both_arms = TRUE), n providers needed total.

Expected acceptance probability comparison group (e.g. Medicaid). Must (0, 1) differ p1. NULL, power back-calculated n; n must provided. Either p2 n must non-NULL. n Integer NULL. Known simple (unclustered) sample size per group. NULL, \(n\) solved p1, p2, alpha, power. Either p2 n must non-NULL. icc Numeric. Intraclass correlation coefficient capturing within-physician clustering. Must \([0, 1)\). Default 0.05. m Numeric. Average number mystery calls placed per physician (cluster size). Must \(\geq 1\). title: Clustered binary power and sample-size calculator (GLMM / VIF approach) — mysterycall_power_calc
code: # Solve for n: Medicaid acceptance (p2 = 0.50) vs commercial (p1 = 0.70) mysterycall_power_calc(p1 = 0.70, p2 = 0.50) #> mysterycall_power_calc: n_simple=91, n_adjusted=105, VIF=1.150, power=80.3% #> $n_simple #> [1] 91 #>  #> $n_adjusted #> [1] 105 #>  #> $vif #> [1] 1.15 #>  #> $p1 #> [1] 0.7 #>  #> $p2 #> [1] 0.5 #>  #> $alpha #> [1] 0.05 #>  #> $power #> [1] 0.803184 #>  #> $icc #> [1] 0.05 #>  #> $m #> [1] 4 #>  #> $message #> [1] "Assuming an acceptance probability of 70% in the reference group and 50% in the comparison group, with an intraclass correlation of 0.050 and an average of 4.0 calls per physician (VIF = 1.150), 91 participants per group are required before clustering adjustment and 105 per group after adjustment, yielding 80.3% power at a two-sided alpha of 0.050 (Donner & Klar 2000)." #>   # Larger ICC and more calls per physician inflate the adjusted n mysterycall_power_calc(p1 = 0.70, p2 = 0.50, icc = 0.15, m = 6) #> mysterycall_power_calc: n_simple=91, n_adjusted=160, VIF=1.750, power=80.3% #> $n_simple #> [1] 91 #>  #> $n_adjusted #> [1] 160 #>  #> $vif #> [1] 1.75 #>  #> $p1 #> [1] 0.7 #>  #> $p2 #> [1] 0.5 #>  #> $alpha #> [1] 0.05 #>  #> $power #> [1] 0.803184 #>  #> $icc #> [1] 0.15 #>  #> $m #> [1] 6 #>  #> $message #> [1] "Assuming an acceptance probability of 70% in the reference group and 50% in the comparison group, with an intraclass correlation of 0.150 and an average of 6.0 calls per physician (VIF = 1.750), 91 participants per group are required before clustering adjustment and 160 per group after adjustment, yielding 80.3% power at a two-sided alpha of 0.050 (Donner & Klar 2000)." #>   # 90% power and a smaller effect require a larger sample mysterycall_power_calc(p1 = 0.70, p2 = 0.55, power = 0.90) #> mysterycall_power_calc: n_simple=214, n_adjusted=247, VIF=1.150, power=90.0% #> $n_simple #> [1] 214 #>  #> $n_adjusted #> [1] 247 #>  #> $vif #> [1] 1.15 #>  #> $p1 #> [1] 0.7 #>  #> $p2 #> [1] 0.55 #>  #> $alpha #> [1] 0.05 #>  #> $power #> [1] 0.9004637 #>  #> $icc #> [1] 0.05 #>  #> $m #> [1] 4 #>  #> $message #> [1] "Assuming an acceptance probability of 70% in the reference group and 55% in the comparison group, with an intraclass correlation of 0.050 and an average of 4.0 calls per physician (VIF = 1.150), 214 participants per group are required before clustering adjustment and 247 per group after adjustment, yielding 90.0% power at a two-sided alpha of 0.050 (Donner & Klar 2000)." #>   # Back-calculate power for a fixed simple n of 100 per group mysterycall_power_calc(p1 = 0.70, p2 = 0.50, n = 100) #> mysterycall_power_calc: n_simple=100, n_adjusted=115, VIF=1.150, power=83.9% #> $n_simple #> [1] 100 #>  #> $n_adjusted #> [1] 115 #>  #> $vif #> [1] 1.15 #>  #> $p1 #> [1] 0.7 #>  #> $p2 #> [1] 0.5 #>  #> $alpha #> [1] 0.05 #>  #> $power #> [1] 0.8386379 #>  #> $icc #> [1] 0.05 #>  #> $m #> [1] 4 #>  #> $message #> [1] "Assuming an acceptance probability of 70% in the reference group and 50% in the comparison group, with an intraclass correlation of 0.050 and an average of 4.0 calls per physician (VIF = 1.150), 100 participants per group are required before clustering adjustment and 115 per group after adjustment, yielding 83.9% power at a two-sided alpha of 0.050 (Donner & Klar 2000)." #>

title: Predict appointment probability for new patient profiles — mysterycall_predict_appointment

Column containing subspecialty label derived exclusively board certification data (e.g. ABOHNS certification_type parsed mysterycall_parse_certification_subspecialty()). DAC NPPES columns must passed subspecialty purposes. default Character scalar. "uninformative" label triggers tier-2 tier-3 logic. Default "General". source_col Character scalar. title: Generate a complete manuscript results report from a fitted model — mysterycall_results_report
code: set.seed(42) df <- data.frame(   wait    = rpois(60, 21),   ins     = rep(c("Medicaid", "BCBS"), 30),   phys    = rep(paste0("Dr", 1:10), each = 6),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) fit <- mysterycall_poisson_model(df, "wait", "ins", "phys") #> Fitting Poisson GLMER: wait ~ ins + (1 | phys) #> boundary (singular) fit: see help('isSingular') #> Convergence issues detected: #>   boundary (singular) fit: see help('isSingular') #> Consider simplifying predictors or using nAGQ = 1. #> Singular fit: random-intercept variance is ~0. The physician-level random effect explains little variation. #> Model fitted: n=60, physicians=10, AIC=371.7, overdispersion=1.16 report <- mysterycall_results_report(   fit,   baseline_mean = 21,   exposure_col  = "ins",   ref_group     = "BCBS" ) print(report) #> === Mystery-Caller Results Report === #>  #> -- Combined Results Table -- #>         Term  IRR IRR 95% CI p-value Days Diff Days 95% CI Significance #>  insMedicaid 1.01  0.90-1.12   0.912      +0.1 -2.0 to 2.5              #>  #> -- Results Paragraph -- #> In multivariable Poisson regression, ins was significantly associated with #> appointment wait time (see Table X). Compared with BCBS, callers presenting as #> Medicaid had an IRR of 1.01 (95% CI 0.90-1.12; p = 0.912) for appointment wait #> time. #>  #>  #> -- Absolute Day-Difference Sentences -- #>   Medicaid-insured callers waited a mean of 0.1 more days compared with BCBS (95% CI 2.0 to 2.5 days; IRR 1.01; p = 0.912).  #>

text: data data frame containing columns referenced outcome_col, random_intercept, candidate_cols. outcome_col Character scalar. Name outcome column. family = "poisson" "nb" must non-negative integer count; family = "logistic" must 0/1 two-level factor. random_intercept Character scalar. Name grouping column physician-level random intercept (e.g. "physician" "last"). candidate_cols Character vector NULL. Columns screen. NULL, columns data used except outcome_col, random_intercept, columns listed exclude_cols. exclude_cols Character vector. Columns always skip, regardless candidate_cols. Default character(0). family Character scalar. Model family: "poisson" (default), "nb" (negative binomial via glmmTMB), "logistic" (binomial logit). alpha_screen Numeric scalar. Liberal p-value threshold used flag "significant" predictors output table. Default 0.20 (appropriate variable selection, confirmatory inference). conf_level Numeric scalar (0, 1). Confidence level Wald intervals. Default 0.95. min_levels Integer scalar. Predictors fewer min_levels unique non-NA values skipped. Default 2L. verbose Logical. TRUE, prints one-line progress message fitting predictor. Default FALSE. max_predictors Integer scalar. Maximum number predictors fit; screening stops many attempts (skipped predictors count toward limit). Default 100L.

NA fitting failed predictor skipped. ci_lower Numeric. Lower confidence bound (exponentiated). ci_upper Numeric. Upper confidence bound (exponentiated). p_value Numeric. Two-sided Wald p-value. p_fmt Character. Formatted p-value ("< 0.001" "0.XXX"). n_levels Integer. Number unique non-NA values observed column. significant Logical. TRUE p_value < alpha_screen. skipped Logical. TRUE predictor fitted (levels, error fitting). skip_reason Character. Explanation skipped = TRUE; NA_character_ otherwise. Rows sorted p_value ascending (skipped rows last). n_screened Integer. Number predictors actually fitted (skipped). n_significant Integer. Number fitted predictors p_value < alpha_screen. family Character. family argument used. sentence Character. plain-language summary suitable Methods Results section. significant_predictors Character vector predictor names p_value < alpha_screen.

title: Screen candidate predictors for a GLMM outcome — mysterycall_screen_predictors

Fits lme4::glmer() (Poisson binomial) glmmTMB::glmmTMB() (negative binomial), wrapped tryCatch(). Extracts coefficient first non-intercept term, exponentiates obtain IRR Wald confidence interval. Labels result "significant" p < alpha_screen.

title: Screen candidate predictors for a GLMM outcome — mysterycall_screen_predictors

title: Side-by-side sensitivity table of exposure-term estimates across models — mysterycall_sensitivity_table
code: # ---- Build fake model objects with structure() — no lme4 required --------  # Model 1: unadjusted logistic (only insurance) m1 <- structure(   list(     or_table = data.frame(       term        = c("(Intercept)", "insuranceMedicaid"),       or          = c(3.50, 0.62),       ci_lower    = c(2.10, 0.40),       ci_upper    = c(5.80, 0.97),       p_value     = c(0.0001, 0.036),       p_value_fmt = c("< 0.001", "0.036"),       stringsAsFactors = FALSE     ),     n   = 160L,     aic = 210.4   ),   class = "mysterycall_logistic_model" )  # Model 2: adjusted (insurance + practice setting) m2 <- structure(   list(     or_table = data.frame(       term        = c("(Intercept)", "insuranceMedicaid", "settingAcademic"),       or          = c(3.20, 0.65, 1.18),       ci_lower    = c(1.80, 0.42, 0.79),       ci_upper    = c(5.70, 1.01, 1.77),       p_value     = c(0.0003, 0.055, 0.417),       p_value_fmt = c("< 0.001", "0.055", "0.417"),       stringsAsFactors = FALSE     ),     n   = 160L,     aic = 208.1   ),   class = "mysterycall_logistic_model" )  # Model 3: adjusted + insurance x setting interaction m3 <- structure(   list(     or_table = data.frame(       term        = c("(Intercept)", "insuranceMedicaid",                       "settingAcademic",                       "insuranceMedicaid:settingAcademic"),       or          = c(3.10, 0.68, 1.21, 0.85),       ci_lower    = c(1.70, 0.43, 0.80, 0.51),       ci_upper    = c(5.60, 1.07, 1.84, 1.42),       p_value     = c(0.0005, 0.094, 0.371, 0.530),       p_value_fmt = c("< 0.001", "0.094", "0.371", "0.530"),       stringsAsFactors = FALSE     ),     n   = 160L,     aic = 209.7   ),   class = "mysterycall_logistic_model" )  tbl <- mysterycall_sensitivity_table(   models        = list("Unadjusted" = m1,                        "Adjusted"   = m2,                        "+ Interaction" = m3),   exposure_term = "insuranceMedicaid",   digits        = 2L ) print(tbl) #>           Characteristic                Unadjusted                  Adjusted #> 1 insuranceMedicaid (OR) 0.62 (0.40–0.97), p=0.036 0.65 (0.42–1.01), p=0.055 #> 2            Sample size                     N=160                     N=160 #> 3                    AIC                     210.4                     208.1 #>               + Interaction #> 1 0.68 (0.43–1.07), p=0.094 #> 2                     N=160 #> 3                     209.7  # ---- Mixed model types: logistic + Poisson side by side ------------------- m_poisson <- structure(   list(     irr_table = data.frame(       term        = c("(Intercept)", "insuranceMedicaid"),       irr         = c(18.3, 1.41),       ci_lower    = c(14.1, 1.08),       ci_upper    = c(23.7, 1.84),       p_value     = c(0.0001, 0.012),       p_value_fmt = c("< 0.001", "0.012"),       stringsAsFactors = FALSE     ),     n   = 145L,     aic = 893.6   ),   class = "mysterycall_poisson_model" )  tbl2 <- mysterycall_sensitivity_table(   models        = list("Offered appt (OR)" = m2,                        "Wait days (IRR)"   = m_poisson),   exposure_term = "insuranceMedicaid",   digits        = 2L ) print(tbl2) #>      Characteristic         Offered appt (OR)           Wait days (IRR) #> 1 insuranceMedicaid 0.65 (0.42–1.01), p=0.055 1.41 (1.08–1.84), p=0.012 #> 2       Sample size                     N=160                     N=145 #> 3               AIC                     208.1                     893.6

title: Simple Poisson Regression for Group Comparison of Count Outcomes — mysterycall_simple_poisson
text: Coxe, S., West, S. G., & Aiken, L. S. (2009). analysis count data: gentle introduction Poisson regression alternatives. Journal Personality Assessment, 91(2), 121–136. Cameron, . C., & Trivedi, P. K. (2013). Regression Analysis Count Data (2nd ed.). Cambridge University Press.

title: Simple Poisson Regression for Group Comparison of Count Outcomes — mysterycall_simple_poisson
code: set.seed(1) df <- data.frame(   days      = rpois(120, lambda = 12),   insurance = rep(c("BCBS", "Medicaid", "Medicare"), 40) ) result <- mysterycall_simple_poisson(df, "days", "insurance",                                      reference = "BCBS",                                      outcome_label = "business days until appointment") #> Fitting simple Poisson GLM: days ~ insurance cat(result$summary_statement) #> Simple Poisson regression was used in place of Kruskal-Wallis because business days until appointment is a count outcome (non-negative integers). Poisson regression models the incidence rate ratio (IRR) directly, which is more interpretable than a rank-based test statistic for count data. The baseline rate (BCBS) is estimated at 11.93 events. For Medicaid compared to BCBS, the business days until appointment rate is approximately 1.03 times higher (3% higher; 95% CI: 0.91-1.17, p 0.676). For Medicare compared to BCBS, the business days until appointment rate is approximately 1.03 times higher (3% higher; 95% CI: 0.91-1.17, p 0.653). print(result$irr_table) #>                term    level      irr  ci_lower ci_upper   p_value p_value_fmt #> 1 insuranceMedicaid Medicaid 1.027254 0.9055750 1.165365 0.6759184       0.676 #> 2 insuranceMedicare Medicare 1.029350 0.9074831 1.167672 0.6527383       0.653 #>   direction #> 1    higher #> 2    higher

Verify random intercepts are stated in methods. #> [WARN] Item  9  Methods: Overdispersion addressed (NB model or test reported) #>          Poisson model detected; verify that overdispersion test/phi is reported in methods. #> [WARN] Item 10  Results: Flow diagram or N screened/excluded reported #>          Verify that a participant flow diagram or exclusion table is included. #> [WARN] Item 16  Discussion: Limitations discussed #>          Cannot auto-detect; verify manually. #> [PASS] Item  7  Methods: Statistical methods: model family specified #>          Model class 'mysterycall_poisson_model' detected; model family is unambiguous. #> [PASS] Item 11  Results: Number of observations with missing data reported #>          model_result$n_dropped = 4. #> [PASS] Item 12  Results: IRR with 95% confidence intervals reported #>          ci_lower and ci_upper columns found with non-NA values in irr_table. #> [PASS] Item 13  Results: p-values reported for primary comparisons #>          p_value column with non-NA values found in irr_table. #> [PASS] Item 14  Results: Overdispersion statistic (phi) reported #>          model_result$overdispersion = 1.300. #> [PASS] Item 15  Results: Sensitivity analysis performed #>          sensitivity_run=TRUE supplied by caller. #>  #> Summary: 6 PASS, 10 WARN, 0 FAIL

NA_real_ crossover undefined, .e., regression slope \(\ge 1\) (diverging) \(\le 0\) (consistent direction). slope Numeric scalar.  Regression slope \(m\). intercept Numeric scalar. title: Compute the wait-time equalization (crossover) point between two insurance groups — mysterycall_wait_time_crossover
text: Beyond crossover point, group2 patients experience longer waits group1 patients (\(0 < m < 1\) crossover exists). Crossover formula. regression line \(y = m x + b\).  Setting \(y = x\) (45-degree line) solving gives \(x = b / (1 - m)\).  finite, positive crossover requires \(0 < m < 1\): \(m \ge 1\): regression line never crosses y = x; group2 wait times diverge group1. \(m \le 0\): relationship non-positive; meaningful equalization point exists. log_transform = TRUE regression operates \(\log(\text{days})\); crossover solved log scale returned \(\exp(x_{\text{cross}})\). Pairing. Observations matched id_col using merge(..., = id_col, = FALSE), physicians appearing insurance groups contribute.  physician one observation per group, observations kept merged natural order subsetting; studies exactly one call per physician per group unambiguous.

title: mysterycall 1.6.0
text: Released 2026-06-25.

title: mysterycall 1.6.0
text: mysterycall_predict_appointment() — generates predicted appointment- acceptance probabilities (plus optional delta-method 95% CIs) new patient practice profiles fitted mysterycall_logistic_model object. Population-level predictions (re.form = NA) default, appropriate new practices unseen model training. mysterycall_enrich_npi() — end--end NPI enrichment pipeline: validates NPIs, looks clinician data, genderizes first names, classifies practice setting, assigns ACOG/census regions. Returns deduplicated data frame. mysterycall_parse_redcap_labels() — parses REDCap data-dictionary choice labels tidy data.frames matching scenario × insurance × NPI patterns used mystery-caller study designs. mysterycall_calendar_sensitivity() — side--side comparison wait-time LMMs fit calendar days vs. business days, reporting coefficient deltas flagging results differ meaningfully two timescales. medicaid_expansion data object — 51-row KFF-sourced dataset recording state’s Medicaid expansion status (adopted / adopted) use stratified analyses.

title: mysterycall 1.6.0
text: broom-compatible tidy() methods added mysterycall_lmm, mysterycall_logistic_model, mysterycall_poisson_model result objects via generics package (now Imports). mysterycall_lmm() — auto log-transform now reports geometric-mean ratios (GMR) confidence intervals alongside standard coefficient table. assign_region() — factor inputs now silently coerced character rather erroring; non-character, non-factor input gives clear error. mysterycall_get_clinician_data() — duplicate columns dropped column-binding prevent cbind errors API responses overlap base data frame columns. caller_reliability() — emits warning() (error) fewer 30 complete pairs found, noting ICC kappa estimates unreliable small n. mysterycall_table1() — gains .data.frame() S3 method results can piped directly flextable knitr::kable(). bizdays fallback — mysterycall_business_days() now falls back calendar days message() instead stop()-ing bizdays package installed.

title: mysterycall 1.6.0
text: Fixed namespace-locking bug test suite: 37 test files calling library(mysterycall) inside devtools::test(), locked package namespace silently broke subsequent with_mocked_bindings() calls. calls removed. Fixed 11-digit NPI generation regression-match-rate mocks n > 10 (changed paste0("123456789", 0:(n-1)) sprintf("1%09d", seq_len(n))). Corrected ACOG district Texas: District XI (VII).

title: mysterycall 1.4.0
text: CRAN-readiness fixes. R CMD check ---cran now passes zero errors, zero warnings, standard “New submission” NOTE. Highlights: Stripped install.packages('X') instructions ~70 error messages. Replaced ggforce::geom_circle mysterycall_plot_source_venn() base-ggplot2 geom_polygon implementation (ggforce dep). Replaced tigris::fips_codes example hardcoded vector (tigris dep). Fixed 301/404 URLs (developer portal, ACGME, USDA ERS). Soft-fail mysterycall_preflight_check() optional Suggests missing. Vignettes guard chunks use Suggests-deps requireNamespace(). rOpenSci alignment. R/ filenames lowercased (ACOG_Districts.R, Splitting_dataframe_to_send_to_callers.R, cityStateToLatLong.R, states_where_physicians_were_NOT_contacted.R → snake_case equivalents). 12 publication/green-journal theme palette functions now carry mysterycall_ prefix (e.g., mysterycall_theme_green_journal(), mysterycall_palette_publication()). Suggests dependency reduction. Dropped four unused packages (imager, leaflet.extras, tmap, tigris) plus ggforce. Suggests count: 48 → 43. Documentation hygiene. devtools::document() now runs cleanly; data documentation converted trailing-string-literal pattern universal @name + NULL pattern. New tests added R/academic_indicators.R R/audit-verify.R. ORCID R-version badges added README pkgdown index.

text: Package renamed mysterycall mysterycall. library(mysterycall) longer work; use library(mysterycall). 100 exported functions now carry mysterycall_ prefix (e.g., mysterycall_geocode(), mysterycall_search_and_process_npi()). previous mysterycall_ prefix names retained deprecated shims emit warning forward new name. even-older unprefixed names (e.g., check_normality()) continue work double-deprecated shims.

title: mysterycall 1.3.0
text: Data quality validation mysterycall_validate_phone() — validates US phone numbers NANP structural rules (NPA/NXX first-digit constraints, N11 service codes) optionally checks area code belongs provider’s reported practice state via bundled lookup table. Returns tidy data frame phone_e164_valid, phone_npa, phone_state_from_npa, phone_area_code_matches_state, phone_validity_flag columns. Fully vectorised; lookup table lazy-loaded cached per session. mysterycall_parse_physician_name() — converts free-text physician name strings (board certification data, NPPES, CMS sources) structured first / middle / last / suffix / title fields confidence scoring (high / medium / low) warning flags. Handles credential vs. Vietnamese surname disambiguation ("Robert Smith " → suffix ""; "Linda " → last name ""), three-part comma format ("Smith, John, Jr."), hyphenated names, name particles. mysterycall_validate_parsed_names() — extends parse output quality flags: has_first, has_last, is_valid, last_is_credential, last_is_suffix, last_too_short, middle_has_particle, quality_issue. mysterycall_format_physician_name() — reassembles parsed components "last_first", "first_last", "formal" display strings; vectorised. mysterycall_test_name_parser() — runs 13-case edge-case accuracy suite prints per-case report console. extended 30-case benchmark corpus available inst/extdata/name_benchmark_corpus.csv; evaluation script data-raw/benchmark_name_parser.R. Safe join wrappers mysterycall_safe_left_join() — wraps dplyr::left_join() key-type harmonisation, right-side uniqueness assertion, coverage threshold enforcement (min_coverage, default 0.98), row-multiplication guard (max_duplication, default 1.02×), optional CSV audit report. mysterycall_safe_inner_join() — wraps dplyr::inner_join() guards; default min_coverage = 0.90. mysterycall_safe_semi_join() — wraps dplyr::semi_join() keep-rate threshold; default min_coverage = 0.50. mysterycall_safe_anti_join() — wraps dplyr::anti_join() -exclusion cap (max_matched, default 1.0). mysterycall_assert_unique_keys() — asserts specified columns form unique key; optionally deduplicates (first row kept) instead erroring. Package infrastructure humaniformat moved Suggests → Imports; runtime requireNamespace() guard removed. 119 new test_that blocks across three new test files (test-validate-phone.R, test-parse-physician-name.R, test-join-safety.R). Five new vignettes: data-quality, statistical-analysis, provider-classification, workflow-orchestration, table-generation. CITATION.cff updated full abstract, keywords, affiliation. CONTRIBUTING.md expanded full developer guide.
